```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(Stat2Data)
data("Clothing")
```

A data frame with 60 observations on the following 8 variables.

ID	Case ID

Amount	Net dollar amount spent by customers in their latest purchase from this retailer

Recency	Number of months since the last purchase

Freq12	Number of purchases in the last 12 months

Dollar12	Dollar amount of purchases in the last 12 months

Freq24	Number of purchases in the last 24 months

Dollar24	Dollar amount of purchases in the last 24 months

Card	1 for customers who have a private-label credit card with the retailer, 0 if not

```{r}
myClothes <- Clothing
```


4.Research question and context. State the research question your final analysis addresses and give enough

### Writeup

  From the given datasets, our group selected the Clothing data set from Stat2Data, which contains 60 observations of 8 variables, collected from a large clothing retailer. This clothing retailer offers a store credit card. Our given data records the use of these cards, as well as variables on frequency, recency of latest purchase, and money spent in the past 12 and 24 months. In this, we would like to purpose the question of how much a customer would spend in their next purchase, based off of the usage of these private-label cards? 

```{r}

mlr.model <- lm(Dollar24 ~ Freq24 + Card, data = myClothes)
summary(mlr.model)
mlr.conf <- augment(mlr.model, myClothes, interval = 'confidence')
summary(mlr.conf)

max(myClothes$Amount)
mean(myClothes$Amount)
median(myClothes$Amount)

max(myClothes$Dollar24)
mean(myClothes$Dollar24)
median(myClothes$Dollar24)
```

  In investigating our data, we looked for any unusual purchase amounts within the dataset. In comparing the max, mean, and median, the range difference is significantly notable. In considering the explanatory variable, dollars spent in most recent purchase (Amount), there is an oustanding outlier with a purchase of \$1,506,000. However, the median amount spent in most recent purchase is \$70. This demonstrates a significantly skewed mean of \$25201.07. 
  
  
```{r}

mlr.model <- lm(Amount ~ Recency + Card, data = cleaned.clothes)
summary(mlr.model)
mlr.conf <- augment(mlr.model, cleaned.clothes, interval = 'confidence')

mlr.confidence <- cleaned.clothes %>%
  mutate(fitted.vals = mlr.conf$.fitted) %>%
  mutate(lower.ci = mlr.conf$.lower) %>%
  mutate(upper.ci = mlr.conf$.upper)


cleaned.clothes <- myClothes %>%
  filter(Amount < 100000)

ggplot(myClothes, aes(x = Recency, y = Amount)) +
  facet_wrap(~Card)
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = as.factor(Card))) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm')+
  labs(title = "Months since Most Recent Purchase vs Price of Most Recent Purchase",
         subtitle = "Dirty Data")

ggplot(cleaned.clothes, aes( x = Recency, y = Amount)) +
  facet_wrap(~Card)
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = as.factor(Card))) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm')+
  labs(title = "Months since Most Recent Purchase vs Price of Most Recent Purchase",
         subtitle = "Cleaned Data")

```
